name: How does home orientation affect sunroom design?

mainEntity.name: How does home orientation affect sunroom design?

acceptedAnswer.text: The orientation of your sunroom dictates how much heat, glare, and daylight it receives throughout the day. South-facing sunrooms capture maximum sunlight all day, which helps warm the space in winter but demands high-efficiency Low-E glass to prevent overheating in summer. East-facing rooms catch bright morning light with shaded afternoons, making them ideal for breakfast spaces. North-facing additions receive consistent, gentle daylight with minimal direct solar heat gain, while west-facing spaces receive intense late-afternoon sun that often requires solar shades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Orientation changes solar exposure: southern exposure maximizes all-day sun, eastern provides gentle morning light, and western exposures require extra shading against afternoon heat.
